findings.subject: apex/salis/doctype/wash_platform/wash_platform.py WashPlatform.validate()
findings.reason: The docstring claims 'validate() guards the mandatory Platform Name'. It does not. WashPlatform.validate() does exactly one thing - `if self.platform_name: self.platform_name = self.platform_name.strip()`. The ValidationError the test catches comes entirely from reqd: 1 on platform_name plus autoname: field:platform_name in wash_platform.json, i.e. stock Frappe mandatory-field machinery, which would raise identically with no controller at all. So the file's only test asserts framework behaviour under a false attribution, and the one behaviour the controller actually implements - trimming, so the stored value matches the name Frappe derives from it - is untested. Fix by re-pointing the assertion at the trim. Not a trim action (removing the only method would empty the file) and not delete (the subject is alive).

findings.subject: apex.salis.utils.get_driver_for_user credential-vs-session resolution
findings.reason: Module-level imports all resolve: apex.salis.utils exports get_driver_for_user and get_driver_for_session_user; apex.salis.api.driver_portal is a live package whose __init__ defines _find_driver and _resolve_driver and imports get_driver_for_user (so patch.object on it is valid); boarding._driver_for_user and its imported get_driver_for_user exist; portal_token_security.BAD_TOKEN_WINDOW_KEY and masar_worker_token.issue_driver_link exist. Two methods reference attributes that are gone. (1) test_fleet_trips_endpoint_ignores_foreign_driver_cookie calls fleet_employee.get_my_recent_trips, which does not exist anywhere in apex/ -- fleet_employee.py defines only get_context, get_my_vehicle, get_fuel_stations, submit_fuel_request and get_my_fuel_requests; the sole remaining mention is a string literal in apex/www/test_portal_shell_contract.py. (2) test_dispatch_permission_hook_ignores_foreign_driver_cookie calls permissions.dispatch_trip_has_permission(trip, 'read', user=...), but apex/salis/permissions.py has only the private _dispatch_trip_has_permission(doc, user=None) at line 547, reached through the DOCUMENT_RULES['dispatch_trip'] lambda at line 722 -- wrong name and wrong arity. Both raise AttributeError. Drop those two methods; the remaining ~18 cover a live credential/session security boundary (patch targets elsewhere are collaborators such as bound_vehicle and frappe.get_all, never get_driver_for_user itself in the tests that exercise it). The two delegation tests that patch get_driver_for_user are asserting the alias delegates, where the alias -- not the helper -- is the subject, so they are not MOCKS-THE-SUBJECT.

findings.subject: habitat room generator / checkout / custody / duplicate-overlap controllers
findings.reason: Drop test_4c_two_issues_same_article_employee (lines 296-307). It wraps the act in `except Exception as e` and then only prints the outcome — there is no assertion of any kind, so it is green whether the second Custody Issue is accepted or rejected, and green if _issue() breaks entirely. Every OTHER except-block in this file (lines 176, 211, 270, 289, 339, 367, 404) binds a flag that is asserted immediately after, which is the legitimate 'did the guard reject' shape and must stay. All imports resolve: submit_via_workflow (_helpers.py:98), ApexHabitatTestCase (factories.py:29), generate_rooms_and_beds (building.py:240), post_stock_entry (accommodation_stock_ledger.py:103).

findings.subject: shipped Workspace JSON name/label/title invariant
findings.reason: Three of the four methods are live and valuable (non-vacuity probe, name==label==title, parent_page resolves to a shipped title). Drop test_rename_patch_ships_and_runs_pre_model_sync (lines 114-135) and its two constants (lines 39-44). It asserts os.path.exists on apex/patches/v2_0/rename_fleet_workspace_to_title_case.py BEFORE it can reach its (properly-worded) skipTest — and apex/patches/ has no v2_0 directory, the string rename_fleet appears nowhere under apex/, and patches.txt does not register it. So the method fails hard today rather than skipping. The rename it was scaffolding for has already landed declaratively: apex/salis/workspace/fleet/fleet.json ships name, label and title all equal to 'Fleet', which the surviving test_name_label_and_title_are_identical already enforces. Nothing is lost by removing it.
